Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian passenger vehicle market is witnessing aggressive commercial realignment as major automotive manufacturers and authorized dealership networks push inventory clearance programs. Industry data tracked by Cartoq.com reveals substantial price revisions, exchange incentives, and direct cash discounts aimed at buyers looking for maximum value on high-demand models including Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Historically, November and December present the most lucrative window for automotive buyers in India. Dealerships face stringent fiscal targets and floor-plan interest costs on unsold stock. To prevent carrying inventory into the new calendar year—which triggers an immediate 1-year registration depreciation perception—manufacturers roll out cumulative benefits combining consumer cash discounts, corporate bonuses, and exchange top-ups.

However, savvy buyers must inspect the fine print carefully before finalizing a deal. Dealerships frequently inflate the on-road quotation by adding compulsory accessory packages (Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000), inflated dealer-level insurance premiums, and arbitrary 'handling or logistics charges'—which have been repeatedly ruled illegal by consumer forums and state transport authorities.

In terms of long-term financial math, purchasing a previous model-year vehicle at a direct cash discount of Rs 1.5 to Rs 2 Lakh easily offsets the nominal 5% to 8% resale value differential if you intend to retain the vehicle for 4 to 6 years. Furthermore, buyers can legally purchase comprehensive motor insurance independently from online aggregators, easily saving an additional Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 compared to showroom quotes.

Our buyer recommendation: visit multiple authorized dealer showrooms in your city, request an itemized price breakdown excluding optional accessories and handling fees, and negotiate matching dealer discounts during the closing week of the month when sales managers are eager to meet monthly volume quotas.

In terms of long-term financial math, purchasing a previous model-year vehicle at a direct cash discount of Rs 1.5 to Rs 2 Lakh easily offsets the nominal 5% to 8% resale value differential if you intend to retain the vehicle for 4 to 6 years. Furthermore, buyers can legally purchase comprehensive motor insurance independently from online aggregators, easily saving an additional Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 compared to showroom quotes.

Our buyer recommendation: visit multiple authorized dealer showrooms in your city, request an itemized price breakdown excluding optional accessories and handling fees, and negotiate matching dealer discounts during the closing week of the month when sales managers are eager to meet monthly volume quotas.

summary: The road transport ministry is studying a plan to link motor insurance premiums to traffic violations. Here's what the proposal means for vehicle owners.
article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: All-New Mahindra BE 07 Electric SUV Arriving Next Year – Key Info
title: All-New Mahindra BE 07 Electric SUV Arriving Next Year
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Mahindra BE 07 electric SUV is expected in India by June 2027 and recent prototype sightings suggest the possibility of a seven-seater derivative Mahindra could soon have two electric SUVs that appeal to families in need of three rows of seats. The XEV 9S already serves that segment and photographs of a BE 07 prototype that surfaced on lately suggest the presence of a third row. Earlier spy images had revealed a five-seat interior and the possibility of two cabin layouts cannot be ruled out. The BE 07 will be the second model under Mahindra’s dedicated BE electric vehicle brand after the BE 6. The original concept debuted in August 2022 and Mahindra had initially planned to introduce its production counterpart in October 2026. The product roadmap disclosed in November now lists an unnamed electric SUV due by the end of June 2027. The BE 07 is expected to occupy that slot. The BE 07 concept had a wheelbase of 2,775 mm which was identical to that of the BE 05 concept. However, its overall length of 4,565 mm made it 195 mm longer. The exterior width and height stood at 1,900 mm and 1,660 mm respectively. Whether Mahindra has altered those dimensions for the production model is yet to be established. Spy Source: SearchEV/Instagram Battery options could mirror those of the BE 6 Sporteq since both SUVs share the INGLO platform. The smaller model currently offers three capacities of 59 kWh, 70 kWh and 79 kWh. Its rear axle motor develops up to 286 PS and 380 Nm while the largest battery provides an MIDC certified range of 708 km. The BE 07 could return a different range due to variations in weight and aerodynamics. Visually, the BE 07 has a more upright rear profile than the coupe styled BE 6. The prototypes have pronounced wheel arches and the tail lamps feature C-shaped illumination elements. The roof spoiler and extended rear section distinguish the silhouette. Mahindra has retained much of the angular design that characterised the original concept. On the inside, photographs of test vehicles have revealed provisions for three displays on the dashboard. The arrangement could resemble that of the XEV 9e and give the front passenger a screen of their own. Other anticipated features are a glass roof, a dashcam, multicolour ambient lights and Level 2 driver assistance technology. The homegrown brand’s original technical outline for INGLO specified lithium iron phosphate cells and DC charge rates of up to 175 kW. The architecture permits either rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. Whether the BE 07 will be available in a dual motor guise will depend on how Mahindra positions it relative to its other electric SUVs.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

Furthermore, buyers can legally purchase comprehensive motor insurance independently from online aggregators, easily saving an additional Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 compared to showroom quotes.

Our buyer recommendation: visit multiple authorized dealer showrooms in your city, request an itemized price breakdown excluding optional accessories and handling fees, and negotiate matching dealer discounts during the closing week of the month when sales managers are eager to meet monthly volume quotas.

Updated Mahindra Thar Roxx Launched in July 2024, the Mahindra Thar Roxx is set to receive a small round of updates soon. Reports say Mahindra plans to equip the new Thar Roxx with the new DaVinci (DCx valve-based) dampers of the Thar OG, a revision that could improve ride quality and stability. Like in the new 3-door Thar, Mahindra will combine the DCx valves with Ride Refine RC1 frequency-dependent valves into the dampers of the new Thar Roxx. The former should manage the slower body movements, and the latter should manage the high-frequency body movements from road undulations. 2. Mahindra XEV 9e Sporteq The Mahindra XEV 9e, the brand’s most expensive electric car, is set to get a few updates on 8 December. The revised version will reportedly be called Mahindra XEV 9e Sporteq, matching the nomenclature of the latest BE 6. Mahindra will likely introduce a new, mid-level power-electric variant for the XEV 9e with this update, combining a rear-mounted electric motor that produces 180 kW (241 hp) and 380 Nm of torque with a 70 kWh LFP battery pack. Charging this battery pack from 20% to 80% will likely take 20 minutes. The new configuration could deliver a range of around 580 kilometres. New software-based features such as karaoke, drift mode, front passenger display parental lock, etc. are also expected to be added with this update. 3. Mahindra plans to launch it before March, and could showcase it at Auto Expo 2027 in February. The company could be targeting a maximum range of around 700 kilometres for this model. 4. Priced from under Rs. 19.79 lakh (ex-showroom), this model will be targeted at outdoorsy customers as well as customers looking for a dual-purpose workhorse. article_paragraphs: The Indian passenger vehicle market is witnessing aggressive commercial realignment as major automotive manufacturers and authorized dealership networks push inventory clearance programs. Industry data tracked by Cartoq.com reveals substantial price revisions, exchange incentives, and direct cash discounts aimed at buyers looking for maximum value on high-demand models including Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Historically, November and December present the most lucrative window for automotive buyers in India. Dealerships face stringent fiscal targets and floor-plan interest costs on unsold stock. To prevent carrying inventory into the new calendar year—which triggers an immediate 1-year registration depreciation perception—manufacturers roll out cumulative benefits combining consumer cash discounts, corporate bonuses, and exchange top-ups.

However, savvy buyers must inspect the fine print carefully before finalizing a deal. Dealerships frequently inflate the on-road quotation by adding compulsory accessory packages (Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000), inflated dealer-level insurance premiums, and arbitrary 'handling or logistics charges'—which have been repeatedly ruled illegal by consumer forums and state transport authorities.

In terms of long-term financial math, purchasing a previous model-year vehicle at a direct cash discount of Rs 1.5 to Rs 2 Lakh easily offsets the nominal 5% to 8% resale value differential if you intend to retain the vehicle for 4 to 6 years. Furthermore, buyers can legally purchase comprehensive motor insurance independently from online aggregators, easily saving an additional Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 compared to showroom quotes.

Our buyer recommendation: visit multiple authorized dealer showrooms in your city, request an itemized price breakdown excluding optional accessories and handling fees, and negotiate matching dealer discounts during the closing week of the month when sales managers are eager to meet monthly volume quotas.

Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

article_paragraphs: The Indian passenger vehicle market is witnessing aggressive commercial realignment as major automotive manufacturers and authorized dealership networks push inventory clearance programs. Industry data tracked by Cartoq.com reveals substantial price revisions, exchange incentives, and direct cash discounts aimed at buyers looking for maximum value on high-demand models including Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Historically, November and December present the most lucrative window for automotive buyers in India. Dealerships face stringent fiscal targets and floor-plan interest costs on unsold stock. To prevent carrying inventory into the new calendar year—which triggers an immediate 1-year registration depreciation perception—manufacturers roll out cumulative benefits combining consumer cash discounts, corporate bonuses, and exchange top-ups.

However, savvy buyers must inspect the fine print carefully before finalizing a deal. Dealerships frequently inflate the on-road quotation by adding compulsory accessory packages (Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000), inflated dealer-level insurance premiums, and arbitrary 'handling or logistics charges'—which have been repeatedly ruled illegal by consumer forums and state transport authorities.

In terms of long-term financial math, purchasing a previous model-year vehicle at a direct cash discount of Rs 1.5 to Rs 2 Lakh easily offsets the nominal 5% to 8% resale value differential if you intend to retain the vehicle for 4 to 6 years. Furthermore, buyers can legally purchase comprehensive motor insurance independently from online aggregators, easily saving an additional Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 compared to showroom quotes.

Our buyer recommendation: visit multiple authorized dealer showrooms in your city, request an itemized price breakdown excluding optional accessories and handling fees, and negotiate matching dealer discounts during the closing week of the month when sales managers are eager to meet monthly volume quotas.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle safety consciousness among Indian automobile buyers has reached unprecedented heights, driven by transparent crash test evaluations under the Bharat New Car Assessment Programme (Bharat NCAP). Verified technical telemetry reported by Cartoq.com provides a detailed examination of structural crashworthiness and passenger protection ratings for Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Under Bharat NCAP protocols, vehicles undergo rigorous offset frontal crash tests at 64 kmph, side mobile deformable barrier impacts at 50 kmph, and stringent pole side-impact evaluations. To secure a coveted 5-star safety rating, a vehicle must achieve high numerical scores in Adult Occupant Protection (AOP) and Child Occupant Protection (COP), while critically demonstrating that the passenger bodyshell remains 'Stable and capable of withstanding further loadings'.

What separates truly crash-resilient vehicles from mere marketing claims is the extensive deployment of advanced high-strength steel (AHSS) and ultra-high-strength hot-stamped steel along the A-pillars, B-pillars, and door sills. Standard fitment of 6 airbags, Electronic Stability Control (ESC), ISOFIX child seat anchorages, and 3-point seatbelts with pre-tensioners across all seating positions has now become the fundamental benchmark for modern Indian buyers.

In real-world highway collisions, vehicles with unstable cabin architectures risk severe footwell intrusion, steering column collapse, and door jamming that traps occupants inside. Indian carmakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra have raised the bar by engineering 5-star crash resilience into their entry and mid-size platforms, compelling global competitors to rapidly upgrade their structural standards.

Our consumer verdict: never compromise on core structural integrity for cosmetic add-ons like ambient lighting or fancy touchscreens. Prioritize vehicles with certified 5-star Bharat NCAP or Global NCAP ratings, verified stable bodyshell integrity, and standard Electronic Stability Program (ESP) to ensure maximum survivability on unpredictable Indian roads.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian passenger vehicle market is witnessing aggressive commercial realignment as major automotive manufacturers and authorized dealership networks push inventory clearance programs. Industry data tracked by Motorbeam.com reveals substantial price revisions, exchange incentives, and direct cash discounts aimed at buyers looking for maximum value on high-demand models including Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Historically, November and December present the most lucrative window for automotive buyers in India. Dealerships face stringent fiscal targets and floor-plan interest costs on unsold stock. To prevent carrying inventory into the new calendar year—which triggers an immediate 1-year registration depreciation perception—manufacturers roll out cumulative benefits combining consumer cash discounts, corporate bonuses, and exchange top-ups.

However, savvy buyers must inspect the fine print carefully before finalizing a deal. Dealerships frequently inflate the on-road quotation by adding compulsory accessory packages (Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000), inflated dealer-level insurance premiums, and arbitrary 'handling or logistics charges'—which have been repeatedly ruled illegal by consumer forums and state transport authorities.

In terms of long-term financial math, purchasing a previous model-year vehicle at a direct cash discount of Rs 1.5 to Rs 2 Lakh easily offsets the nominal 5% to 8% resale value differential if you intend to retain the vehicle for 4 to 6 years. Furthermore, buyers can legally purchase comprehensive motor insurance independently from online aggregators, easily saving an additional Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 compared to showroom quotes.

Our buyer recommendation: visit multiple authorized dealer showrooms in your city, request an itemized price breakdown excluding optional accessories and handling fees, and negotiate matching dealer discounts during the closing week of the month when sales managers are eager to meet monthly volume quotas.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Motorbeam.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

raw_title: Production-Spec Honda Alpha e-SUV Sketches Revealed Ahead Of Debut
title: Production-Spec Honda Alpha e-SUV Sketches Revealed Ahead Of Debut
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Honda Alpha design sketches reveal the electric SUV’s exterior and five-seater cabin a week before its global unveiling in India on December 2 Honda has offered a glimpse of its first locally manufactured electric SUV before the vehicle takes centre stage at an event in India next Wednesday. The two illustrations released today originated at the Honda Design Centre in Japan and depict the Alpha from a front three-quarter angle as well as a side view of its cabin. The finished car will be unveiled on December 2, 2026. From the side, the Alpha looks almost like a cross between an MPV and an SUV. The windscreen sits at a steep angle but the roof stays relatively high towards the tail. The rear pillars are unusually thick and the exterior mirrors sit on the doors below the window line. Black trim around the wheel arches extends along the sills. Inside, the raised centre console incorporates a recess for small items beneath the dashboard. Honda has separated the driver’s instrumentation from the central touchscreen and placed a row of physical controls beneath the latter. The dashboard itself sits low relative to the base of the windscreen. Back in March, Honda flagged off a nationwide road test programme for the Alpha from its Tapukara facility in Rajasthan. By June, a camouflaged prototype had reached Manali. The development programme takes into account variations in road surfaces and climate as well as the availability of charging facilities in different parts of the country. Meanwhile, the rear bench in the sketch features pale upholstery, three individual head restraints and a foldable centre armrest. The slim front seatbacks and flat cabin floor could prove beneficial on longer journeys for three rear passengers. Purple ambient illumination runs along the dashboard and door trim just below the windows. Honda has retained much of the nose design from the 0 Alpha prototype exhibited in Tokyo in October 2025. The new H emblem sits between the lamps inside a dark panel that visually links the front corners. The five-spoke alloy wheels use triangular silver inserts while the lower bumper features a separate air intake. Honda intends to produce the Alpha in Rajasthan for domestic and overseas markets and sales will begin in 2027. Two lithium iron phosphate battery options of around 65 kWh and 75 kWh have been reported but the figures are speculative. Prices could start at Rs. 16 lakh (ex-showroom) and the SUV will compete directly against the Hyundai Creta Electric, Mahindra BE 6, Tata Sierra EV, and Maruti Suzuki e Vitara.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Gaadiwaadi.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: First Clear Look: Maruti Leaked With Major Design Upgrades Inside & Out
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Maruti Suzuki Fronx facelift could debut in early 2027 and the prototype reveals new cabin amenities as well as minor revisions to the exterior Nearly four years after the Fronx made its domestic debut at the 2023 Auto Expo, Maruti Suzuki looks set to introduce its first comprehensive update. The Baleno received a midlife revision in September 2026 and its crossover sibling has since been spotted on public roads on numerous occasions. The photographs from Harsh VLOGS now offer a glimpse inside an automatic test vehicle. Visually, Maruti Suzuki seems to have preserved the characteristic proportions of the Fronx. The sloping roofline, rear quarter glass and alloy wheel design bear similarities to the existing model. Up front, the three individual LED elements sit above the main headlamp clusters while the camouflaged grille and bumper could conceal the bulk of the cosmetic revisions. Perhaps the more consequential changes will occur under the bonnet. The four-cylinder K12N petrol engine could be replaced by the 1.2-litre Z12E three-cylinder unit from the Baleno. In the hatchback, it develops 82 hp and 112.4 Nm. The claimed fuel efficiency stands at 23.80 kmpl for the manual version and 24.77 kmpl for the AMT. Image Source: Harsh Vlogs/Youtube Inside the prototype, the absence of a traditional handbrake lever immediately draws attention to the revised centre console. Maruti Suzuki has incorporated an electronic parking brake and an Auto Hold function. Two switches near the armrest indicate the availability of individual front seat ventilation. The seats also sport revised leatherette upholstery in black and burgundy. Interestingly, photographs of another prototype last month revealed rear disc brakes and sensors on the front bumper. The potential presence of a radar module behind the grille suggests that the Fronx could receive Level 2 ADAS. The revised Baleno already offers adaptive cruise control, lane departure prevention, automatic emergency braking and high beam assist. Image Source: Harsh Vlogs/Youtube Elsewhere, the dashboard architecture has changed little as the familiar circular instrument dials, central information display and three-spoke steering wheel have survived. Maruti Suzuki could introduce the Clarion audio system and actively cooled wireless smartphone charger from the Baleno. The existing nine-inch infotainment screen and head-up display are also expected to be retained. The Fronx currently costs from Rs. 6.95 lakh (ex-showroom) as per the price revision reported earlier this week. Its 1.0-litre Boosterjet turbo petrol engine develops 100 hp and 147.6 Nm and will presumably survive the facelift. The existing five-speed manual and six-speed torque converter automatic transmissions could be retained too. Maruti Suzuki may unveil the revised crossover at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo in February 2027.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: JSW Motors Unveils Official Logo, First SUV To Debut Next Week
title: JSW Motors Unveils Official Logo, First SUV To Debut Next Week
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - JSW Motors will make its independent debut in India on December 3 and its first SUV is expected to be the Combat equipped with a plug-in hybrid system Just over a week before JSW Group introduces its independent passenger vehicle business in India, the company has revealed the badge that its cars will wear. JSW Motors released a short film yesterday to showcase its emblem for the first time. The official brand launch will take place on December 3, 2026 while prospective owners can already register their interest on the company’s website. The insignia takes its visual inspiration from a wheel in motion and incorporates two distinct elements within an elliptical perimeter. Interestingly, the geometry adheres to the proportions of the golden ratio. The upward sweep of the individual elements symbolises collective progress according to the company. Black and white constitute the primary colour scheme while teal serves as an accent colour. The first model to sport the badge is expected to be the Combat which derives its mechanicals from the Jetour T2 sold internationally. The five-seater SUV could employ a 1.5-litre four-cylinder turbocharged petrol engine in conjunction alongside two electric motors and an 18.4 kWh battery. The plug-in hybrid system could develop around 360 hp and 610 Nm. Power will reportedly reach the front wheels via a three-speed dedicated hybrid transmission. For reference, the overseas specification Jetour T2 has a claimed electric-only range of 90 km as per the NEDC test cycle. article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: Hyundai Gifts New Bayon SUV To Paralympic Champion Sheetal Devi
title: Hyundai Gifts New Bayon SUV To Paralympic Champion Sheetal Devi
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Hyundai has gifted its new Bayon midsize SUV to world champion para archer Sheetal Devi who secured two gold medals and a silver in Japan last month Hyundai Motor India has felicitated Sheetal Devi in Gurugram just weeks after her successful campaign at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The South Korean automaker presented the 19-year-old para archer a new Bayon on November 25. The occasion comes nearly two months after Hyundai appointed the athlete as its brand ambassador. The association between Hyundai and Sheetal dates back to 2023 when the manufacturer initiated its Samarth programme in India. The Hyundai Motor India Foundation has since worked alongside the GoSports Foundation to assist para athletes. Sheetal received the prestigious Arjuna Award in January 2024 after her international success in her debut season. At just 17 years of age, the athlete from Jammu and Kashmir became the youngest Paralympic medallist from India after she secured bronze alongside Rakesh Kumar in Paris. Subsequently, she clinched her maiden individual world championship title in Gwangju, South Korea in September 2025. She defeated Türkiye’s Öznur Cüre Girdi by 146 points to 143 in the compound final. Interestingly, Sheetal retained both her individual and mixed team titles at the Asian Para Games last month. She overcame Singapore’s Nur Syahidah Alim in the individual final and partnered Toman Kumar to defeat Indonesia in the mixed team event. She also secured silver alongside Payal Nag in the women’s compound doubles as her overall medal tally at the continental championships rose to six. As for the Bayon, Hyundai introduced the five-seater SUV in India on October 26, 2026 at Rs. 9.999 lakh (ex-showroom). It sits between the Venue and Creta and is available in seven trim levels namely HX2, HX3, HX3+, HX5, HX6, HX8, and HX10. The 1.5-litre naturally aspirated petrol engine develops 115 PS and 143.8 Nm and can be paired to either a six-speed manual or an iVT. The Bayon measures 4,245 mm in length and has a wheelbase of 2,600 mm. It offers a ground clearance of 205 mm and a boot capacity of 505 litres. Higher specification variants get an electrically adjustable driver seat, ventilated front seats, twin 12.3-inch displays, a Bose audio system and a panoramic sunroof. Furthermore, six airbags and electronic stability control are standard fitments. Hyundai will introduce a factory-fitted CNG derivative of the Bayon in January 2027 and it will consequently become the first midsize SUV from the brand to offer the alternative fuel option in India. The locally manufactured SUV is also destined for more than 50 overseas markets as Hyundai seeks to increase its export volumes.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

This is the fourth time the company has increased prices in calendar year 2026, following the revisions in June, August, and September. article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Gaadiwaadi.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: Next Gen Rexton SUV Teased With Jeep & Range Rover Design Cues
title: Next Gen Rexton SUV Teased With Jeep & Range Rover Design Cues
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - KG Mobility will launch the new Rexton PHEV in South Korea in January 2027 and the flagship SUV will reportedly utilise a monocoque architecture Four years after the Mahindra Alturas G4 disappeared from showrooms in India, its South Korean counterpart is about to undergo a generational change. KG Mobility released the first teaser images of the new Rexton yesterday and confirmed that the SUV will feature a plug-in hybrid powertrain. Its commercial debut in South Korea will take place in January 2027. The association between Mahindra and the Rexton dates back to October 2012 when the SUV arrived in India under the SsangYong badge. Mahindra had acquired a controlling stake in the South Korean automaker a year earlier. The RX5 manual variant cost Rs. 17.67 lakh while the RX7 automatic version commanded Rs. 19.67 lakh (ex-showroom, Mumbai). Both derived power from a 2.7-litre diesel engine. Six years later, Mahindra introduced the second generation Rexton domestically as the Alturas G4 at an introductory price of Rs. 26.95 lakh (ex-showroom). The seven-seater SUV employed a 2.2-litre diesel engine rated at 178 bhp and 420 Nm. It competed against the Toyota Fortuner and Ford Endeavour and boasted equipment such as ventilated front seats, nine airbags and a 360-degree camera system on the top variant. As for the new Rexton, the rear profile bears a noticeable resemblance to the current generation Range Rover. The black trim on either side of the tailgate houses slender vertical LED elements and discreetly integrated turn indicators. The registration plate sits lower down on the tailgate beneath the prominently displayed Rexton lettering. Meanwhile, the five illuminated grille slots at the front evoke the design of Jeep SUVs. KGM has employed a similar arrangement on its Musso pickup truck but the Rexton gets slimmer headlamp clusters split into two sections. The squared bonnet and angular bumper further differentiate it from the outgoing model. Arguably, the biggest departure from previous Rexton generations lies beneath the bodywork. KGM secured the rights to use Chery Automobile’s T2X architecture in October 2024 and the new SUV reportedly dispenses entirely with its separate ladder frame chassis. The development also marks a mechanical separation from the Musso pickup for the first time in the nameplate’s history. The Rexton PHEV carried the internal project code SE-10 and KGM commenced pilot production last month ahead of final road tests. Details of its battery capacity, electric range and combined power output will emerge from December onwards.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Tata Motors will revise its car and SUV prices for the fourth time in 2026 next month as an average increase of 0.5 per cent takes effect on December 1 The cost of purchasing a new Tata car in India will go up for the fourth time in eight months. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles confirmed earlier today that its entire passenger vehicle range will be subject to a price revision from December 1, 2026. The decision comes at a time when the company has yet to fully recover the extra expenses incurred in vehicle production this year. Tata began the financial year in April 2026 by revising the prices of its petrol, diesel and CNG cars by a weighted average of 0.5 per cent. Subsequently, both ICE and electric models became dearer by up to 1.5 per cent in July before another revision of up to Rs. 25,000 came into effect in September. The December increase will average 0.5 per cent but the payable number will depend on the model and variant. For instance, a uniform application of the announced rate would make the base Nexon dearer by Rs. 3,700 and the Safari by Rs. 6,700. The indicative figures for individual models are tabulated below. The initial acquisition cost of the 45 kWh Nexon EV fell to Rs. 8.99 lakh while the 63 kWh Sierra EV and 65 kWh Harrier EV became available from Rs. 11.99 lakh and Rs. 14.49 lakh respectively. The battery attracts separate charges under this arrangement. Commercially, October 2026 proved fruitful for the homegrown manufacturer as domestic sales rose by 21 per cent to 73,894 units from 61,134 units twelve months ago. The Nexon and Punch collectively represented over 57 per cent of its domestic volumes. Furthermore, Tata dispatched 16,244 electric vehicles to domestic and overseas markets as against 9,286 units in October 2025. Discounts and exchange or scrappage incentives amount to as much as Rs. 1.25 lakh on eligible Curvv variants. The Sierra diesel attracts benefits worth up to Rs. 1.15 lakh while select petrol manual variants of the Nexon qualify for savings of up to Rs. 75,000. Elsewhere in the domestic passenger vehicle market, Maruti Suzuki revised its prices by an estimated weighted average of 0.31 per cent. Hyundai will make select models and variants dearer by up to Rs. 8,000 at the beginning of December. Even the luxury car segment will witness a revision as Audi has announced a price increase of up to 2 per cent from January 1, 2027.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: TVS Jupiter Gets Past A Monumental One Crore Production Milestone In India
title: TVS Jupiter Gets Past A Monumental One Crore Production Milestone In India
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - TVS Jupiter has reached one crore cumulative production units in just 13 years and the second half of that volume took only four years to achieve TVS Motor Company rolled out the one croreth unit of the Jupiter from its manufacturing facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu today. According to the manufacturer, the Jupiter has become the youngest scooter nameplate to attain the production record in India. Interestingly, its annual production rate over the past four years was more than twice the average registered in the preceding nine years. Currently, the TVS Jupiter 110 costs between Rs. 74,700 and Rs. 90,525 (ex-showroom) and can be had in Drum, Drum Alloy, SmartXonnect Drum, SmartXonnect Disc and Dual Tone variants. Prices for the Jupiter 125 range from Rs. 82,100 to Rs. 90,335 (ex-showroom, East Delhi). The former uses a 113.3 cc engine producing 5.9 kW and up to 9.8 Nm while the latter develops up to 6.3 kW and 11.1 Nm from its 124.8 cc engine courtesy of iGO Assist. Back in 2013, TVS introduced the Jupiter as an alternative to the established Honda Activa. Within its first year of commercial availability, it became the quickest scooter brand to register five lakh sales. The Jupiter subsequently rose to second position in the domestic scooter market and earned the Scooter of the Year award. Perhaps the biggest transformation in the Jupiter’s history came in August 2024 when the second generation 110 cc scooter arrived. TVS extensively revised its mechanicals and exterior design while the horizontal light bars gave the scooter an entirely different look. Three years prior to that overhaul, TVS had ventured into the 125 cc family scooter category under the Jupiter nameplate. The larger displacement model competes against the Suzuki Access 125 and Honda Activa 125. Its introduction gave TVS a second family scooter at a higher price point alongside the sportier Ntorq 125. Storage space has been one of the differentiating factors of the Jupiter family. The 110 cc model gets a 33-litre underseat compartment sufficient for two helmets while the external fuel filler permits refuelling without the need to lift the seat. Other notable provisions are metal body construction and smartphone connectivity via TVS SmartXonnect on select variants. More recently, TVS introduced the Dual Tone Spectral edition of the Jupiter 110 in August 2026. Besides its colour-shifting paint finish, the scooter features sequential turn indicators, a USB Type-C charging port, colour coordinated inner panels, partially chromed mirrors and an integrated backrest. The edition now sits at the top of the Jupiter 110 range after the withdrawal of the Stardust Black Special Edition.

summary: Mumbai Police Commissioner To Cops: Maintain Your Mahindra Scorpio-N Patrol Cars Or Else....
article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.
